definitions.explanation: Looking worn out, cheap, or in poor condition; giving an impression of poverty or neglect.

examples.japanese: みすぼらしい⟦{服|ふく}→服：00695_fuku⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{着|き}ている→着る：00541_kiru⟧。
みすぼらしい⟦{建物|たてもの}→建物：01458_tatemono⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{並|なら}んでいる→並ぶ：00605_narabu⟧。
⟦{昔|むかし}→昔：01515_mukashi⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{立派|りっぱ}→立派：01093_rippa⟧だった⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{今|いま}→今：00945_ima⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧みすぼらしく⟦なった→なる：01970_naru⟧。
examples.english: It used to be splendid but has become shabby now.

notes:
みすぼらしい describes something that looks shabby, run-down, or poor. It conveys a visual impression of poverty or neglect.

FORMS:
- みすぼらしく⟦ない→ない：01118_nai⟧: not shabby (negative)
- みすぼらしく: shabbily (adverbial)
- みすぼらしかった: was shabby (past)
- みすぼらしさ: shabbiness (noun form)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- みすぼらしい⟦{服|ふく}→服：00695_fuku⟧: shabby clothes
- みすぼらしい⟦{建物|たてもの}→建物：01458_tatemono⟧: run-down building
- みすぼらしい⟦{格好|かっこう}→格好：01800_kakkou⟧: shabby appearance
- みすぼらしく⟦なる→なる：01970_naru⟧: to become shabby

WRITING:
Can be written as {見窄|みすぼ}らしい, but hiragana is standard.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{粗末|そまつ}→粗末：03323_somatsu⟧: plain, humble, shabby (things, food)
- ⟦{貧相|ひんそう}→貧相：18816_hinsou⟧: poor-looking (especially people's appearance)
- ボロボロ: tattered, falling apart (stronger, physical deterioration)
- {古臭|ふるくさ}い: old-fashioned, musty (emphasizes outdatedness)
